messages:
april: heads-up — customer 'GlyphPay' on Dedicated reported that trace view is missing most child spans for a 30m window this morning. They say the root span is there but no downstream spans show and search by x-request-id returns nothing.
jack: can you paste the request id example? and which region / cluster? :thinking:
april: sure — request id `req_20260317_7f9b2a` from cluster eu-west-1-ded-2. Occurred ~2026-03-17T09:12Z. Customer sent a screenshot of the trace pane showing only a single span and a greyed-out timeline.
nina: is this the same pattern as the last week trace pruning bug? that was sampling-related. but that one kept links, just dropped spans at tail. this sounds like the link between request_id -> trace id lookup failed.
april: they tried searching the trace explorer with the request id and got "no results". Console logs (from customer) show the service emitted spans with trace_id headers. I asked for agent logs but wanted us to triage first.
jack: quick checks I'm running now:
- query collector for trace_id / req_20260317_7f9b2a
- check trace-indexer lag metrics
- check agent version on that host pool

jack: collector query returned a parent span doc in ES: trace_id `t_8c1d` present, parent span logged at 2026-03-17T09:12:11Z. child spans don't show up in ES results. indexer lag metric (indexing.delay_seconds) spiked to ~45s for that cluster at 09:12Z but generally is <2s.
april: customer says latency to console was fine but charts under "trace activity" were empty for that interval.
ryan: possible causes: 1) child spans failed to be indexed due to mapping error; 2) a recent change to dedup/linking logic dropped spans that had duplicate (or missing) parent_id; 3) request->trace lookup path uses a secondary index that was temporarily stale.
jack: I pulled the indexer logs — saw repeated bulk rejections around that window with error `mapper_parsing_exception` for field `peer.service` with unexpected type list vs string. that would cause entire bulk to fail and be retried later, so child spans could be delayed/missing until retry. sample log:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:14Z] ERROR bulk_processor - bulk failed: mapper_parsing_exception: failed to parse
  at org.elasticsearch.index.mapper ...
  caused_by: ClassCastException: java.util.ArrayList cannot be cast to java.lang.String
```
nina: why would `peer.service` be a list? we had a client change that allowed multiple backends and started sending `peer.service: ["auth","cache"]` in proto -> maybe not normalized before indexing.
april: customer traces show tags: `peer.service: auth` on parent, but the service emitting child spans (payments) added a multi-value header recently (PR #1427) that might be populating span.attributes incorrectly.
jack: action: I rolled back the indexer mapping rollout for the `peer.service` field to accept arrays (temporary shim) and forced a reindex of failed bulks. I also bumped the bulk retry to 5 and added a 30s backoff to reduce thrash.
ryan: added a quick fix in the receiver to coerce multi-value `peer.service` -> join(',') before enqueuing for indexing. patch on staging, will promote if green.
april: customer wants a timeline + repro so we can explain outage and mitigation. can we list exact repro steps to get missing-links behavior?
jack: repro steps (local):
1) run a service that emits spans with parent_id = p123 and two child spans that include `peer.service` as an array value (simulate PR #1427).
2) send 100 requests quickly to trigger bulk indexing.
3) temporarily introduce a mapping mismatch by setting ES mapping for `peer.service` = "text" (single-valued) then attempt to index docs where `peer.service` is an array -> bulk failures.
4) observe that parent doc indexed (maybe from another worker) but child spans failed bulk and appear missing from trace view until reindex.

nina: additional note — the request_id -> trace lookup path queries a compact traces index keyed by trace_id. If child spans never indexed, the trace timeline shows only root. If the compact index update failed, trace explorer query by request_id may not return since the compact index expects a complete document.
april: good. can we confirm whether the customer's environment had a recent agent version change? they said they applied agent 1.3.2 yesterday.
jack: checking audit logs for eu-west-1-ded-2 — several hosts updated agent -> 1.3.2 at 2026-03-17T02:00Z. That agent introduced a change that serializes `peer.service` as repeated field when multiple backends present. we need to roll a fix to normalize before emit.
ryan: plan:
- immediate: communicate to GlyphPay that we've found bulk-indexing errors caused by multi-valued `peer.service`. we reprocessed failed bulks; most traces from 09:12-09:50 should now show child spans (give them ~15m for full refresh).
- short term (today): release receiver patch to coerce arrays -> string join; adjust indexer mapping permissive; monitor indexing.delay_seconds and mapper_parsing_exception rate.
- medium term: mod agent to emit normalized attributes and add schema validation in the pipeline agent -> collector to drop/normalize bad types with counters.

april: I've drafted a customer message. quick review? "We identified a transient indexing issue caused by multi-valued span attributes which caused bulk indexing failures; we retried and reprocessed the failed bulks and child spans should appear in the trace view now. We're deploying a fix to normalize these attributes at the receiver to prevent recurrence."
jack: 👍 add an internal incident ref: INC-4519 and link to reindex job id `reindex-1763004000-4519` so support can follow.
nina: I'll add a Grafana panel to the support dashboard showing mapper_parsing_exception rate and indexing.delay_seconds so we can alert earlier.
april: customer updated — they see most spans reappearing, timeline looks normal now. they asked for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.
ryan: ETA for receiver patch to prod ~3h if no blockers, agent normalization PR will take ~2 days including tests. include rollback plan in RCA.
april: thanks everyone. I'll send the customer update and close the escalation once they confirm all traces show. leaving follow-ups: @jack reindex job status, @nina alert panel, @ryan prod rollout of receiver patch. :white_check_mark:
